claims.text: Hf15Mo15Ta15Ti20Zr35 processed by arc melting, HIP at 1200°C/200 MPa for 1 hour, and annealing at 1000–1100°C for 24 hours will form discrete coherent B2 precipitates in a continuous disordered BCC matrix.
The B2 precipitates will be Ti/Zr/Hf-rich, whereas the BCC matrix will be Mo/Ta/Hf-rich.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that otherwise cause premature cracking.
Discrete B2 precipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing dislocation motion.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix improves plasticity and avoids the embrittlement associated with a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
Ti addition enhances grain-boundary cohesion and thereby improves ductility.
Optimizing the Ti/Zr ratio and avoiding W and Nb reduces alloy density.
The coherent precipitates can be cut by dislocations or bypassed by Orowan looping without catastrophic interface decohesion.
The proposed alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of 1.2–1.4 GPa.
The proposed alloy will have room-temperature tensile ductility of 10–15%.
The proposed alloy will have a density of 9.8–10.2 g/cm³ and remain below 10.5 g/cm³.
The resulting B2 precipitates will be uniformly distributed and nanoscale.
Conventional equiatomic Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 typically contains a continuous B2 phase or coarse intermetallic networks.
The equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline has yield strength above 1.5 GPa and room-temperature ductility below 5%.
The equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline has a density of approximately 10.5 g/cm³.
Precise control of annealing temperature and time will prevent B2 precipitate coarsening and formation of a continuous B2 network.
The alloy must remain in the BCC+B2 region because shifting too far toward B2 stability will reduce ductility.
Reducing density substantially below 9.5 g/cm³ is unlikely without adding lighter elements such as Al or Mg.
The nominal Hf15Mo15Ta15Ti20Zr35 composition is intended to form a single-phase BCC solid solution after melting.

contradictions.description: The success claim requires yield strength above 1.2 GPa and tensile ductility above 10%, but falsification is triggered only below 1.0 GPa or below 5%. Results of 1.0–1.2 GPa or 5–10% would fail the stated hypothesis while not meeting its falsification rule.
